brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: A tool rack that hangs on a wall
requirements.evidence: One full hex base (piece:0,0,0;full) with a cap on its open face. It is a single-cell rack, about 214 x 80 x 209 mm. Two keyhole hangers on the wall-side faces (slots 0 and 1) let it hang on screws already in a wall. Mount is not tested against a real wall or load.
accessory hex-acc-keyhole at slots 0 and 1 of the base (accessory:0#0,0#0 and accessory:0#0,0#1). check_build is clean with meshClash clear.

Three hook plates (hex-acc-hook, accessory:0#0,0#2/0#3/0#4) on the front faces, each carrying two hooks per the catalog. The configurator's prop library has no hand tool that rests on a hook: only cable coil, gaffer tape and FPV goggles hang there, and gaffer tape was refused for lack of rest. So no tools are shown on the hooks.

requirements.requirement: Material, strength and load of the hooks and mounts
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only. Print material, load rating and wall fixing strength are not verified.

finish.summary: Built a single-cell tool rack: one full hex base with two keyhole hangers on the wall side, three hook plates on the front faces for hand tools, and a cap on the open face. The configurator reports no issues and meshClash is clear. Hook plates have hooks but no hand-tool props can rest on them, so the tools are not shown. Strength and material are not checked.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

parts.name: Hook plate
parts.use: Each plate carries two hooks side by side, so you bolt on as many as you want where you want them rather than committing a whole face to a rail.
